speaker: kathyfisher
text: Thanks, I forgot to put that on the agenda for you under my report. So I attended the culture days and it was a cultural tourism. It was a symposium and there was a panel. So it was Ontario Travel, Destination Northern Ontario, Destination Ontario. It was Jasmina from the Art Gallery, myself from the Irma Tinger. Donna Hillsinger was there on behalf of Fall Festival and the city. The, we spoke about working together on cultural tourism and how to create itineraries and Road Scholar was really our big topic is we didn't identify Road Scholar per se, but we talked about bus tour itineraries and how we work together on a theme. So the last six years, it was group of seven and we're hoping to bring group of seven back again, but we're also now on a new itinerary with this indigenous itinerary where with Peter White and Joe Surrett and then Shinrock. So what was really interesting is someone asked the question, how lucrative is cultural tourism? And after all this work of coordinating and creating a play and live theater and bringing together your menu, the heritage menu and all that, was it worth it? And so I quickly did the math and we did six years. And if we look at just the bus tours only that we brought here and we had public dinners and all of that, I didn't include that. We had 118 in six years of the Road Scholar bus tours. And that at an average of, I just took 30 people on the bus and then times the price we charged them that it came out over six years to $250,000. And I made someone else bring their phone out and calculate it quick too so we could answer this question fast. And that was just to the Irma Tinger site over six years. The art gallery did the same for a group of seven. So I mean, part of that went to the theater troupe and we take out of that a little bit for supplies and our grocery supplies and things, but it was really interesting that when that question came up how we were able to say that we have created cultural tourism on these itineraries. So our presentation was liked so much. We have two invitations possibly coming up for TILE, which is Tourism Industry Association Ontario or something close to that. Their conference is in October and the Ontario Museum Association has asked us to submit as well. So I don't know if we've become the new cultural tourism roadshow or what, but we believe it went very well at least. It was lots of conversation afterwards.
